Export selected native R scientific records in frozen Python 1.2 portable format

etr_export_python_portable_result.Rd

Writes NumPy-compatible scientific arrays, typed JSON dataclass field envelopes, metadata, diagnostics, provenance, units, a SHA256 archive digest, and an explicit R-native source-package version. Paired sparse-MFPCA serialization requires the genuine native joint covariance/PACE estimator; fixed-bandwidth W2 workflows may not request optional audited selector, score uncertainty, or observation diagnostics in this initial portable domain. The Python 1.2 load_portable_result reader can audit the output without reconstructing opaque fitted objects. It does not claim identical Python runtime objects, Python environment capture, arbitrary dataclass support, or independent scientific certification.

Usage

etr_export_python_portable_result(result, directory,
    include_environment = FALSE, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

result

Native common-grid or irregular trajectory collection, dense FPCA/MFPCA scientific fit, compositional FPCA, strict 29-field paired sparse-MFPCA fit, or fixed-bandwidth paired sparse-MFPCA W2 workflow with canonical frozen Python 1.2 scientific fields.

directory

New or empty output directory for arrays.npz and manifest.json.

include_environment

Must be FALSE. An R interpreter cannot honestly provide a Python interpreter environment capture.

overwrite

Must be FALSE. Scientific evidence is not destructively overwritten.

Value

Output directory, invisibly.
